title: Rethinking Back Transformation in 2-stage Eigenvalue Decomposition on Heterogeneous Architectures
problem: 2-stage EVD method loses performance advantage over 1-stage when computing eigenvectors via back transformation on GPUs.
motivation: Back transformation bottleneck limits applicability of efficient 2-stage EVD; need optimization for obtaining eigenvectors.
method: During bulge-chasing (the phase where computation shifts along the matrix diagonal), replace BLAS3 operations—which work on entire matrix blocks—with BLAS2 operations, which work on single vectors. Reorganize the workflow from a fixed backward sequence to a pattern that maximizes GPU parallelism, which hides the latency introduced by the divide-and-conquer decomposition.
key_novelty: The core insight is switching to BLAS2 operations and reorganizing the workflow for GPU parallelism during back transformation (computing the eigenvectors from the decomposition).
contributions: 2.62x vs MAGMA and 2.21x vs cuSOLVER for complete FP64 EVD
